what: The element (a decoration such as a big circle behind a heading) is pulled toward the cursor like a spring. If the distance d between the cursor and the element’s resting center is within a Gaussian range of element width × 1.6 (0 beyond 2.2 times that), it follows the cursor by min(d × .35, width × 10%) on a spring with stiffness 90 and damping 11, and rests once it stops. When the cursor leaves the window it returns to its resting place. Only translate is used, so the element’s own transform is left untouched.

options.reach: Pull range (multiple of element width), default 1.6
options.max: Farthest travel distance (in element widths), default .1
options.pull: Follow ratio relative to cursor distance, default .35
options.bound: So it doesn’t cross the right wall of this ancestor (css) — only up to 75% of the right margin

note: Only on mouse/trackpad (hover: hover · pointer: fine) — not attached on touch
